items.prompt: Given a string of '(', ')', '[', ']', '{', '}', decide whether every bracket is closed in the correct order.
items.why: Nesting: the most recently opened bracket must close first → push openers, pop on closers.

items.prompt: Given daily temperatures, return for each day how many days you must wait for a warmer temperature.
items.why: 'Next greater to the right' for every element → monotonic decreasing stack of indices, answer = i − j on pop.

items.prompt: Return the maximum of every contiguous window of size k as the window slides across the array.
items.why: A fixed-size contiguous window with elements leaving from the left → a sliding window with a monotonic deque. A stack can't drop items from the bottom.

items.prompt: Repeatedly remove pairs of adjacent equal letters from a string until no such pair remains (e.g. 'abbaca' → 'ca').
items.why: A removal can expose a new adjacent pair to its left → compare each char with the top of a stack and pop on a match.

items.prompt: Find the minimum number of moves a knight needs to get from one square to another on a chessboard.
items.why: Fewest moves with unit cost → expand positions in first-in, first-out order with a queue (BFS). A stack (or DFS) goes deep first and finds a path, not the shortest one.

items.prompt: Find the largest rectangle that fits under a histogram of bar heights.
items.why: Each bar's rectangle extends to the previous and next smaller bars → increasing monotonic stack, O(n).

items.prompt: Design a structure that returns the k-th smallest of all numbers seen so far after each insertion.
items.why: 'k-th smallest overall' needs order over all elements, not just the latest one → keep a size-k max-heap.

items.prompt: Compute the total size of a folder, where a folder contains files (with sizes) and other folders nested to any depth.
items.why: The structure is defined in terms of itself: size(folder) = its files + size of each subfolder. Recursion follows that definition directly. A stack or queue could do the same walk, but nothing calls for them here.
